diagnostic_evidence.quote: Plugging it in \cref{eq:indasp} and using mathematical induction, we obtain

issues.failure_explanation: With coefficients on the right, the generalized Bezout theorem places the solvent as the LEFT factor: Phi(lambda)=(lambda I-B)Psi(lambda). The proof peels B_d first, then hat B_{d-1} from Phi_{d-2}, etc., so substituting Phi_{i-1}=(lambda I-hat B_i)Phi_{i-2} into eq:indasp yields prod_{j=i+1}^d(lambda I-hat B_j)(lambda I-hat B_i)Phi_{i-2}, i.e. the new factor lands on the RIGHT. Under the paper's product convention this is not prod_{j=i}^d(...), so the induction does not close: the true factorization is (lambda I-hat B_d)(lambda I-hat B_{d-1})...(lambda I-hat B_2)Phi_0, the reverse of eq:deffp1. Consequently eq:solventS (which multiplies omega_i^T by hat B_{i+1} first) and the forward recurrence for S_{i,j} are computed in the wrong order as well. Concrete check for d=3, b=2: B_3=diag(0,1), B_2=[[2,1],[0,3]] gives hat B_2=[[2,1/2],[0,3]]; the paper's F(X)=(X^2-X hat B_2-XB_3+hat B_2B_3)S^{-1} has F(B_3)=(hat B_2B_3-B_3 hat B_2)S^{-1}=[[0,1/2],[0,0]]S^{-1} != 0 and F(B_2) != 0, so it is not the fundamental matrix polynomial; the reversed product (X^2-XB_3-X hat B_2+B_3 hat B_2) does vanish at both B_2 and B_3. Only d=2 is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the construction: define S_{i,j} by recursing downward from j=d (S_{i,d+1}=I, S_{i,j}=B_iS_{i,j+1}-S_{i,j+1}hat B_j for j=d,...,i+1) and state the factorization as (lambda I-hat B_d)(lambda I-hat B_{d-1})...(lambda I-hat B_2)S_{1}^{-1}; redo eq:solventS in that order and propagate to thm:Chain and the definitions of chi_mono, chi_coef. The norm-based bounds in eq:Gd and thm:sb then go through unchanged in form.
issues.overall_effect: eq:deffp1 and eq:deffp are false for d>=3 as written, so the growth estimate eq:Gd (whose chi quantities are defined from these hat B_i and S_{1,d}) and the bound eq:mainsb of thm:sb (whose G_d is defined via eq:deffp) are unsupported as stated; the remark that only hat B_d=B_d is a solvent is also inconsistent with the displayed order (in the displayed product hat B_2 would be the solvent).
issues.title: Chain factorization formula has wrong factor order; induction step ignores non-commutativity
issues.why_classification: The stated formula and the proof's inductive step are wrong (not a typo: the definitions of S_{i,j} must be changed), but a contained systematic reordering restores every downstream result with the same shape, so no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: c_Omega contains max_j ||Omega_j|| twice, so c_Omega^2 contains that maximum to the fourth power. Union bounds give max_i||Omega_i^{-1}||<=sqrt(b)d/delta, max_j||Omega_j^{-1}||<=sqrt(b)(m-d)/delta and M:=max_j||Omega_j||<=2sqrt(b)+sqrt(2log(2(m-d)/delta)), yielding c_Omega^2<=bd(m-d)*(bd^2/delta^2)*(b(m-d)^2/delta^2)*M^4=(dn-bd^2)^3 M^4/delta^4. The stated bound has M to the first power, which the argument does not deliver and which is smaller than the derivable bound (M>=2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor (2sqrt(b)+sqrt(2log(2(m-d)/delta))) by its fourth power.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit high-probability constant for c_Omega in thm:sb is unsupported as stated; the structural bound eq:mainsb and the qualitative conclusions are unaffected.
issues.title: Probabilistic bound on c_Omega^2 omits the fourth power of the spectral-norm tail term
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a constant/logarithmic factor with no effect on rates, scope, or dependent results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notably, $\Lambda$ may consist of either a cluster of interior eigenvalues or a subset of exterior eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:boundMP bounds ||Phi(B_j)|| by the max of ||Phi(lambda)|| over the whole interval [lambda_j^{(1)},lambda_j^{(b)}] spanned by the eigenvalues of B_j. For an interior cluster, a b x b block Lambda_j of Lambda_perp (fixed by the given decomposition) may contain eigenvalues both below lambda_min^cl and above lambda_max^cl; then [lambda_j^{(1)},lambda_j^{(b)}] contains the cluster interval, and the lemma's max includes lambda inside [lambda_min^cl,lambda_max^cl], where G_d and thm:interpolation give no control. The proof's restriction of the max to [lambda_min,lambda_max] minus the cluster interval is therefore not what the lemma provides.

failure_location.quote: Note that all eigenvalues of $B_{j}$ for $d+1\leq j\leq m$ are in $[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\setminus [\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$, \cref{lem:boundMP} yields that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sharpen lem:boundMP to take the maximum over the finite spectrum {lambda_0^{(1)},...,lambda_0^{(b)}} (its own proof already yields this after the step bounding sum_j phi_j^2(lambda_0^{(j)}) by b max_j sum_l phi_l^2(lambda_0^{(j)})), or reorder Lambda_perp so that no block straddles the cluster.
issues.overall_effect: As written, eq:mainsb is not established for interior clusters whenever some block Lambda_j has eigenvalues on both sides of the cluster interval, the regime emphasized in rmk:sb.
issues.title: Lemma on ||Phi(B_j)|| applied with the wrong lambda-range when a block of Lambda_perp straddles the cluster interval
issues.why_classification: A short local strengthening of the lemma (already implicit in its proof) closes the gap with no loss in the theorem's conclusion or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $d = 1$, \cref{cor:eig} recovers the convergence result for randomized single-vector Lanczos method from \cite[Thm.~3.1]{kressner2024randomized}.

issues.failure_explanation: thm:sb plus conj:chi give tan(angle) <= c_Omega (chi/relgap)^{d-1}. Folding the dimension-dependent factor c_Omega into the (d-1)-th power is only possible for d>=2; for d=1 the stated right-hand side equals 1 (and relgap is a min over an empty index set), whereas G_1=||F_1||=1 and tan(angle(range Q, range Omega))=||Omega_perp Omega_1^{-1}|| is typically of order sqrt(n)>>1. Hence the corollary is false for d=1, and the follow-up claim that eq cor:eig with d=1 (which then reads tan<=1/Cheb_{l-1}(...)) 'recovers' the single-vector result of [kressner2024randomized, Thm 3.1] (which carries a dimension/probability-dependent prefactor) is incorrect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound as c'_{b,d,n} (c_{b,d,n}/relgap)^{d-1} (or restrict to d>=2), and correspondingly include the prefactor in eq cor:eig and in the remark about d=1.
issues.overall_effect: The d=1 instance of conj:sb and of eq cor:eig is false; the d>=2 content and the comparison to the single-vector case must be restated with an explicit prefactor.
issues.title: Conjectured corollary absorbs c_Omega into (c/relgap)^{d-1}, giving a false bound for d=1
issues.why_classification: Only a degenerate boundary case and a comparison remark are wrong; a one-factor restatement preserves all intended content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory

issues.failure_explanation: The paper asserts chi_mono <= max_i ||B_i|| ||B_i^{-1}|| for d=2. Counterexample: lambda_min^cl=1, Lambda_1=diag(1,1+eps), Omega_1=[[1,t],[0,1]] gives B_1=[[1,-t eps],[0,1+eps]], so ||I-B_1||/||I-Lambda_1|| = sqrt(1+t^2), while B_1=I+eps*N with ||eps N||=eps sqrt(1+t^2); taking eps sqrt(1+t^2)=0.1 gives ||B_1|| ||B_1^{-1}|| <= 1.1/0.9 while the ratio (hence chi_mono) is >= sqrt(1+t^2), arbitrarily large. The correct elementary bound is chi_mono <= max_i ||Omega_i|| ||Omega_i^{-1}|| (since lambda I - B_i = Omega_i^{-1}(lambda I - Lambda_i)Omega_i), not the condition number of B_i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by chi_mono <= max_{i=1,2} ||Omega_i|| ||Omega_i^{-1}||, which is bounded by Gaussian singular-value tail bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed inequality in the 'intrinsic challenge' discussion is false; the qualitative message (chi_mono is controllable by random-matrix bounds while chi_coef is hard) survives with the corrected bound via kappa(Omega_i).
issues.title: Claimed bound chi_mono <= max kappa(B_i) for d=2 is false
issues.why_classification: An isolated false auxiliary inequality in an illustrative discussion with an immediate correct replacement and no dependents.
